items.title: Weatherproofing for Any Season
items.summary: Each season in New England brings with it a unique set of challenges when it comes to the comfort and energy efficiency of your home. While it’s important to stay on top of seasonal changes, like sealing drafty windows with heat-shrink plastic, there are ways to save money year round by weatherproofing – regardless of the current season. We’ve rounded up 10 of the best tips to start you on your way.

items.title: Reduce Energy Usage, Not Holiday Fun
items.summary: The holiday season is full of bright lights, festive meals, and chilly weather. All that holiday revelry can impact your household's energy usage, but that's no reason to summon your inner Scrooge.

items.title: I Can't Pay My Utility Bill...Now What?
items.summary: Unitil takes great pride in safely and reliably delivering gas and electricity to our customers while also providing affordable and sustainable energy solutions. Should you find yourself experiencing financial hardship, we have a number of resources that can help you take control of your expenses with budget billing, payment plans, and assistance from local community agencies.

items.title: How to Make the Most Out of Your Heat This Winter
items.summary: Keep the Heat In – and the Cold OutHarness the power of the sun by opening the curtains to take advantage of the greenhouse effect, allowing the sun to naturally heat your home. Of course, windows – older, single-paned windows in particular – can also be a significant source of heat loss, so be sure to close the curtains once the sun has set.

items.title: Get the Most out of your Ceiling Fans
items.summary: If you use air conditioning to cool your home, a ceiling fan will allow you to raise the thermostat setting about 4°F with no reduction in comfort.

items.title: How Animals Impact Our Electrical Infrastructure
items.summary: Wildlife and electrical infrastructure share the same space, and that relationship has an impact on electric reliability. Animals can cause outages by chewing on lines, building nests on equipment, or creating unintended electrical paths. At Unitil, wildlife is responsible for roughly 13%* of power outages across our service territory, making it a common cause of service interruptions. Most animal-related outages occur in the spring and the fall when animals are most active.

While Unitil does not provide customers with solar panels, we allow (and in fact, encourage!) you to generate your own renewable energy in parallel with our electric system.
